blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 9 sold over 5 months against an average of 14.6 listed, about 8.1 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was August with 3 sold. Condos and townhomes: 7 sold over 5 months against an average of 6.8 listed, about 4.9 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was October with 3 sold.

blocks.text: Lots and land in The Crest

items.t: Established house lots: A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Lot character, only: typical Crest lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level (no official source read states them). The applicable R1 SSMUH thresholds are a 281 m² minimum lot area and a 10 m minimum lot width, with unit counts turning on the 280 m² / 281 m² and 400-metre frequent-transit thresholds in. These are district thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot.

: Burnaby's R1 district allows lots with two or more primary units to be stratified — a multiplex lot can become strata lots. Where that happens, each resulting lot IS strata tenure (Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply). That is a development outcome under the zoning, not an existing bare-land strata plan in The Crest: no existing bare-land strata plan in The Crest was verified.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a garbage toter fee, with the detached single-family water charge at $652.33 and sewer for single-family homes billed as a sewer parcel tax — servicing for any single parcel is confirmed with the City, not confirmed parcel by parcel here.
ALR vs non-ALR: parcel-level ALR status: Not verified; no ALR percentage split is stated. Check any parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Streamside position: Byrne Creek drains the wider Edmonds area south to the Fraser River, and parcel-level streamside setbacks are property-specific checks: Not verified for individual lots. No area-wide flood or hazard designation for The Crest was found in the sources read.
No bare-land strata plan in The Crest was verified

No named bare-land development, assembly, development site or rezoning proposal inside The Crest is documented: — the research states that a market residential presale inside The Crest verified on a developer source is not verified (none confirmed). None is carried as for-sale inventory. The Edmonds Community Plan covers the town centre plan area west of The Crest; it is a plan for Edmonds ground, not a Crest lot development.

Historic subdivision fabric = built lot fabric, not offerings: the East Burnaby side streets are established fee-simple lot fabric documented above; no historic subdivision is presented as a lot offering.
: No named presale project of any form inside The Crest was confirmed on an official or developer source.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around The Crest

items.t: The Crest surrounds The Crest Centre, around 10th Avenue, 6th Street and Edmonds Street in south-east Burnaby, with the New Westminster border at the east edge; exact MLS® boundary streets: Not verified. Nearby: Edmonds town centre to the west, East Burnaby and Cariboo to the north, New Westminster across the municipal border to the east and south-east. "Crestdale" is a historical local name for this part of East Burnaby — its current official status: Not verified.

Roads and transit: 10th Avenue, 6th Street, Edmonds Street and Kingsway serve the area. Edmonds Station (Expo Line) is west of the sub-area and is its SkyTrain link; no SkyTrain station sits inside The Crest. Bus route numbers for Crest streets: Not verified. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Parks, recreation, library and care: Robert Burnaby Park is in the wider East Burnaby area north of the sub-area; park facility detail for The Crest itself: Not verified beyond that. No City recreation centre sits inside the sub-area in the sources read. Burnaby Public Library's Tommy Douglas Branch, 7311 Kingsway, serves this quadrant from Edmonds. Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, is the city's hospital; the Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #201-7315 Edmonds St.

Shopping: The Crest Centre is the local neighbourhood plaza the sub-area is named for; its owner, anchor tenant and store list were not confirmed on an official source: Not verified. The City-designated town centre serving the area is Edmonds, west on Kingsway.

Market context, labelled correctly: SnapStats covers Burnaby. Community context only (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only; land has NO SnapStats category): Burnaby Detached median $1,825,000, $662/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 37 days; Burnaby "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $686,000, $763/sqft, 98%, 36 days. Sub-area medians: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in The Crest

items.t: Subdivision + servicing — Burnaby servicing-bylaw BASE number HELD not confirmed: the servicing bylaw was renamed by Amendment Bylaw No. 14667, 2024, and no base number is asserted here and none is invented; the documented process instead: new homes and SSMUH projects require Engineering pre-application approval through My Permits Portal before a building permit application, and where offsite servicing requirements are identified in the Pre-Approval Report, a cash-in-lieu contribution to City infrastructure is required, calculated on Engineering unit rates. Confirm subdivision and servicing requirements with the City for the parcel.

Bare-land strata block (for the form — no Crest bare-land strata plan is verified; it applies to any R1 multiplex stratification): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Crest ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31).

blocks.text: Good to know about The Crest

items.t: Burnaby's zoning changed under this sub-area in 2026: Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 and the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) replaced the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan maps — a Crest document citing Bylaw No. 4742 or the 1998 OCP is citing superseded instruments.

The transit test is worth units: the jump from 4 homes to 6 turns on a lot of at least 281 m² sitting within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop — two similar Crest lots can carry different multiplex value purely on that measurement.

The plaza names the sub-area, not the City: "The Crest" matches The Crest Centre plaza; City use of the name as an official neighbourhood was not confirmed, and its owner, anchor and store list are not verified — sell the verifiable anchors (Edmonds Station, Tommy Douglas Branch, the two elementaries), not an official-neighbourhood claim.

faq.a: Burnaby — south-east Burnaby on the Edmonds / East Burnaby side near the New Westminster border.
faq.q: Is The Crest in Vancouver or Burnaby?

faq.a: No verified one — the sub-area is established fee-simple houses, no bare-land subdivision or presale lot offering was verified, and the verified strata stock is built townhouses on Cumberland Street / Cumberland Place.
faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in The Crest?

faq.a: Under the R1 SSMUH district: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop — with a 10 m minimum width and 281 m² minimum area for SSMUH lots.
faq.q: How many homes can a Crest house lot hold?

faq.a: Yes on the City's wording: lots with two or more primary units may be stratified — and once stratified, each lot is strata tenure with Form B, fees and bylaws.
faq.q: Can a multiplex on a Crest lot be sold unit by unit?

faq.a: None is quoted here: Burnaby's servicing-bylaw base number is HELD not confirmed (renamed by Amendment Bylaw No. 14667, 2024). The documented route is Engineering pre-application approval through My Permits Portal, with cash-in-lieu for offsite works identified in the Pre-Approval Report.
faq.q: What servicing number governs a Crest subdivision?
Where is The Crest in Burnaby?
faq.a: In south-east Burnaby on the Edmonds / East Burnaby side, around 10th Avenue, 6th Street and Edmonds Street near the New Westminster border; "The Crest" is the GVR MLS® sub-area name and matches the local Crest Centre plaza (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: Which schools are in or near The Crest?
faq.a: Second Street Community Elementary (K–7), 7502 2nd St, and Morley Elementary (K–7), 7355 Morley St, with Byrne Creek Community Secondary (8–12), 7777 18th St, the nearest secondary on the Province's SD41 list; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the SD41 locator.
